claude.sample_unit: operative notes (5 procedures x 4 authorship conditions), reviewed by 10 blinded otolaryngologists

links.outcome: Approval rate of operative notes: GPT-only versus attending-edited hybrid (attending plus GPT)
links.effect: Hybrid attending+GPT notes had the highest 'as is' approval rate (79%), versus 23% for GPT-only notes, which had the most omissions and overdocumentation.
links.quote: Hybrid notes written by an attending surgeon with GPT assistance received the highest average domain scores and the highest "as is" approval rate (79%), outperforming all other groups.

links.effect: Hybrid attending-plus-GPT notes had the highest average domain scores and 79% “as is” approval, outperforming all other groups.
links.quote: Hybrid notes written by an attending surgeon with GPT assistance received the highest average domain scores and the highest "as is" approval rate (79%), outperforming all other groups.

links.outcome: GPT and hybrid versus clinician-authored notes
links.effect: Hybrid attending-plus-GPT notes had the highest average domain scores and 79% approval; GPT-only had the lowest approval rate, 23%.
links.quote: Hybrid notes written by an attending surgeon with GPT assistance received the highest average domain scores and the highest "as is" approval rate (79%), outperforming all other groups.

links.effect: Hybrid human-AI collaboration outperformed AI-only authorship; hybrid approval was 79%, while GPT-only approval was 23%.
links.quote: In this limited dataset, hybrid human-AI collaboration outperformed both human-only and AI-only authorship in operative documentation.

links.outcome: operative note quality and approval rate
links.effect: Hybrid notes with attending and GPT achieved the highest approval rate (79%) and domain scores, outperforming GPT-only notes which had a 23% approval rate and the highest incidence of omissions and overdocumentation.

screen.practice: Attending surgeon review/editing of GPT-drafted operative notes (human-in-the-loop)
screen.reason: Empirical study comparing clinician-alone, AI-alone, and hybrid clinician-reviewed AI generation for operative notes, directly testing the impact of clinician-in-the-loop review on quality and approval.

primary.practice: clinician review and editing of AI-generated documentation
